note: Weft-knit structures, grouped by the four base families. Our wording. All terms are proposals awaiting review.

terms.label: Single jersey
terms.definition: Every needle knits on one bed; all loops are drawn to the same side.

terms.label: Plated jersey
terms.definition: Single jersey knitted with two yarns in the same loops, one kept on the face and one on the back.

terms.label: Tuck jersey
terms.definition: Single jersey with tuck stitches: a needle takes yarn without casting off its loop.

terms.label: Float jersey
terms.definition: Single jersey with missed needles, so the yarn floats past them on the back.

terms.label: Eyelet jersey
terms.definition: Single jersey with loops transferred to a neighbouring needle, leaving holes.

terms.label: 1×1 rib
terms.definition: Both beds knit, alternating one wale on each.

terms.label: 2×2 rib
terms.definition: Both beds knit, alternating two wales on each.

terms.label: Half cardigan
terms.definition: Rib in which one bed tucks on alternate courses.

terms.label: Full cardigan
terms.definition: Rib in which the beds tuck in turn on alternate courses.

terms.label: Milano rib
terms.definition: A course of rib followed by one course on each bed alone.

terms.label: 1×1 purl (garter)
terms.definition: Courses alternate between the beds, so face and back loops alternate course by course.

terms.label: Interlock
terms.definition: Two 1×1 ribs knitted into each other on alternate needles, smooth on both sides.

terms.label: Punto di Roma
terms.definition: A course of interlock followed by one course on each bed alone.

terms.label: Double jacquard
terms.definition: Two or more yarns: the face shows a picture, the back bed knits a backing.
